q: 1. A vessel of 4 m³ contains an oil which weights 30 kN. The specific weight of the oil is
explain: Specific weight = Total Weight / Total Volume = 30 kN / 4 m³ = 7.5 kN/m³.

q: 2. The pressure intensity in kN/m² (or kPa) at any point in a liquid is
explain: Pressure (P) is the product of specific weight (w) and depth (h).

q: 3. The pressure at a point 4 m below the free surface of water is
explain: P = wh = 9.81 kN/m³ * 4 m = 39.24 kN/m² (kPa).

q: 4. A manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: While differential manometers measure pressure differences, a standard manometer (like a U-tube) is used for point pressure in pipes/channels.

q: 5. A differential manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: The specific purpose of a differential manometer is to determine the pressure head difference between two distinct points.

q: 6. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall per unit length is
explain: P = w * Area * x̄. For unit length (1m) and depth H, Area = H * 1 and x̄ = H/2. Thus, P = wH²/2.

8. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will float if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: A body floats when its weight is less than or equal to the maximum possible upthrust (weight of the fully displaced volume).

q: 9. The buoyancy depends upon the
options: pressure with which the liquid is displaced
explain: According to Archimedes' Principle, the magnitude of the buoyant force is exactly equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

q: 10. The metacentric heights of two floating bodies A and B are 1 m and 1.5 m respectively. Select the correct statement
options: The bodies A and B have equal stability
The body A is more stable than body B
The body B is more stable than body A
The bodies A and B are unstable
explain: Stability of a floating body is directly proportional to its metacentric height (GM). A higher GM provides a larger restoring couple.

q: 11. The time of oscillation of a floating body is given by
explain: The time period (T) formula is T = 2π√(k² / (GM·g)), where k is the radius of gyration and h (or GM) is the metacentric height.

q: 12. One cubic metre of water weighs
explain: By standard metric definition, 1 cubic metre (m³) of volume is equivalent to 1000 litres of liquid.

q: 13. The imaginary line drawn in the fluid in such a way that the tangent to any point gives the direction of motion at that point, is known as
explain: A streamline is a curve that is everywhere tangent to the local velocity vector of the fluid flow.

q: 14. The frictional resistance of a pipe varies approximately with ............ of the liquid.
explain: According to Froude's experiments on fluid friction, for turbulent flow, the frictional resistance is proportional to the square of the velocity ($v^2$).

q: 15. The pressure of fluid due to hammer blow is ............
options: directly proportional to density of fluid
inversely proportional to density of fluid
explain: Water hammer pressure $P = ho v C$, where $C$ (velocity of pressure wave) involves $\sqrt{K/ho}$, making $P$ proportional to $\sqrt{ho}$.

q: 16. When a cylindrical vessel containing liquid is revolved, the surface of the liquid takes the shape of ............
explain: The free surface of a liquid in a forced vortex takes the shape of a paraboloid of revolution.

q: 17. The total pressure on the top of a closed cylindrical vessel completely filled up with a liquid is ............
explain: By integrating the pressure over the top surface area, the total force (or pressure) is found to be proportional to $R^4$.

q: 18. When a cylindrical vessel of radius (r) containing liquid is revolved about its vertical axis ω rad/s then depth of parabola which the liquid assumes is ............
explain: The height of the paraboloid (rise at the edges) is given by $Z = v^2/2g = \omega^2 r^2 / 2g$.

q: 19. The unit of dynamic viscosity in S.I. units is ............
explain: Dynamic viscosity ($\mu$) in SI units is Pascal-seconds (Pa·s), which is equivalent to $N \cdot s/m^2$.

q: 20. One poise is equal to ............
explain: 1 Poise = 1 dyne-s/cm² = 0.1 N·s/m² (or 0.1 Pa·s).

q: 21. The kinematic viscosity is the ............
options: ratio of absolute viscosity to the density of the liquid
ratio of density of the liquid to the absolute viscosity
product of absolute viscosity and density of the liquid
product of absolute viscosity and mass of the liquid
explain:
Kinematic viscosity ($
u$) is defined as $\mu/ho$.

q: 22. The viscosity of water at 20°C is ............
explain: At 20°C, the dynamic viscosity of water is approximately 1.0 centipoise (0.001 Pa·s).

q: 23. A fluid which obeys the Newton's law of viscosity is termed as ............
explain: By definition, Newtonian fluids follow the linear relationship $	au = \mu (du/dy)$.

q: 24. When a tank containing liquid moves with an acceleration in the horizontal direction, then the free surface of the liquid ...............
explain: Due to horizontal acceleration, the liquid surface tilts. The depth increases at the rear (back) end and decreases (falls) at the front end.

q: 25. Bulk modulus of a fluid is the ratio of ...............
options: increase in volume to the viscosity of fluid
increase in pressure to the volumetric strain
critical velocity to the viscosity of fluid
explain: Bulk modulus (K) measures a fluid's resistance to compression and is defined as the ratio of compressive stress (pressure increase) to volumetric strain.

q: 26. The value of bulk modulus of a fluid is required to determine ...............
explain: The Mach number relates flow velocity to the speed of sound, which itself is calculated using the Bulk Modulus (K) and density (ρ).

q: 27. Mercury is generally used in barometers because ...............
options: its vapour pressure is practically zero
the height of the barometer will be les
explain: Mercury's high density allows for a manageable column height (~760mm), and its low vapor pressure prevents error in the vacuum space.

q: 28. The depth of the centre of pressure on a vertical rectangular gate (4 m wide, 3 m high) with water upto top surface is ...............
explain: For a rectangle of height 'h' with the top at the surface, the center of pressure is at (2/3)h. (2/3) * 3m = 2.0m.

q: 29. When a body is totally or partially immersed in a fluid it is buoyed up by a force equal to ...............
options: weight of the fluid displaced by the body
weight of the body and fluid displaced by the body
difference of weights of the fluid displaced and that on the body
explain: This is Archimedes' Principle, which defines the buoyant force as the weight of the volume of fluid that the body displaces.

q: 30. A water tank partially filled with water is being carried on a truck moving with a constant horizontal acceleration. The level of the water ...............
options: rises on the front side of the tank
falls on the back side of the tank
remains the same at both sides of the tank
rises on the back side and falls on the front side
explain: The inertia of the water causes it to move toward the rear of the tank, resulting in a higher water level at the back and a lower level at the front.

q: 31. The imaginary line drawn such that the tangents at its all points indicate the direction of the velocity of the fluid particles at each point, is called ...............
explain: A streamline is a curve that is everywhere tangent to the instantaneous local velocity vector.

q: 32. The acceleration f required to accelerate a rectangular tank containing water horizontally so that the slope of its free surface is 45°, is ...............
explain: Since tan θ = a/g, and tan 45° = 1, then a/g = 1, which means the acceleration (f) must equal g.

q: 33. A fluid particle may possess the displacement or ...............
explain: Fluid motion can involve translation (moving), rotation (spinning), and deformation/distortion (changing shape).

q: 34. A jet projected at an angle of 45°, 40 m from the foot of a vertical column, just reaches the top of the column. The height of the column is ...............
explain: Using the trajectory equation y = x tanθ - [gx² / (2u² cos²θ)]. For a project reaching its max height at 40m distance at 45°, the height is 20m.

q: 35. A piezometer opening in pipes measures ...............
explain: A piezometer tube measures the static pressure (P/w) at the point of connection.

q: 36. An open container filled with water is moved vertically downward with a uniform linear acceleration. The pressure at its bottom will be ...............
explain: The effective acceleration becomes $(g - a)$. Therefore, the pressure $P = ho(g-a)h$, which is less than the static pressure.

q: 37. Shear stress is directly proportional to ...............
explain: According to Newton's Law of Viscosity, shear stress ($	au$) is directly proportional to the velocity gradient ($dv/dy$).

q: 38. Poise is the unit of ...............
explain: Poise is the CGS unit of dynamic viscosity ($1 Poise = 0.1 N\cdot s/m^2$).

q: 39. Kinematic viscosity (ν) is equal to ...............
explain:
Kinematic viscosity is the fluid's resistance to flow under gravity, defined as $
u = \mu / ho$.

q: 40. Monometer is a device used for measuring ...............
options: velocity at a point in a fluid
pressure at a point in a fluid
explain: A manometer is a simple device that uses a column of liquid to measure the pressure at a specific point in a fluid system.

q: 41. Differential manometers are used for measuring ...............
options: velocity at a point in a fluid
pressure at a point in a fluid
difference of pressure between two points
explain: Differential manometers are specifically designed to measure the pressure drop or difference between two distinct points in a pipeline.

q: 42. The centre of pressure for a plane vertical surface lies at a depth of ...............
explain: For a vertical rectangular surface starting at the liquid surface, the centre of pressure is located at $2/3$ of the total depth ($H$).

q: 43. Flow of a fluid in a pipe takes place form ...............
explain: Fluid flow is always driven by the gradient of total energy (head). Fluid moves from points of high total energy to low total energy.

q: 44. A submerged body will be in stable equilibrium if ...............
explain: For a fully submerged body, the centre of buoyancy ($B$) must be above the centre of gravity ($G$) for stability.

q: 45. The meta-centric height (GM) is given by ...............
explain: Mathematically, $GM = BM - BG$, where $BM = I/V$. Therefore, $GM = (I/V) - BG$.

q: 46. If the density of a fluid is constant from point to point in a flow region, it is called
explain: Incompressible flow is a flow where the density of the fluid remains constant throughout the flow process.

q: 47. If the fluid particles move in straight lines and all the lines are parallel to the surface, the flow is called
explain: Laminar flow (also known as streamline flow) is characterized by fluid particles moving in smooth, parallel layers or 'laminae'.

q: 48. For a sub-merged curved surface, the component of force due to static liquid is equal to
options: weight of the liquid supported by curved surface
force on a projection of the curved surface on a vertical plane
area of curved surface × pressure at the centroid
explain: The vertical component of hydrostatic force on a curved surface is equal to the weight of the liquid vertically above the curved surface up to the free surface.

q: 49. The square root of the ratio of inertia force to pressure force is known as
explain: The Euler number is the square root of the ratio of the inertia force to the pressure force.

q: 50. Model analysis of aeroplanes and projectile moving at super-sonic speed are based on
explain: For high-speed flows where compressibility effects are significant (supersonic), the Mach number is the primary similarity parameter used for model testing.

q: 51. The drag force exerted by a fluid on a body immersed in the fluid is due to
explain: Drag is the combined effect of shear stress (viscous force) and the pressure distribution (pressure force) acting on the surface of the body.

q: 52. Numerical value of gauge pressure is
explain: Absolute Pressure = Gauge Pressure + Atmospheric Pressure. Therefore, gauge pressure is always less than absolute pressure by the amount of atmospheric pressure.
